Preston, Amon & Efstathiou (2305.09827) find that to reconcile DES Y3 cosmic shear with Planck LCDM, the non-linear suppression needed is weaker than the KiDS-1000 value (A_mod ~ 0.69). It is still more extreme than recent hydrodynamic simulations predict, and it must extend into the mildly non-linear regime, to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. The DES Y3 A_mod value itself was not in the text I read (abstract and conclusions), so it remains unsourced.

Second mitigation method (Maraio, Hall & Taylor, 2410.12500): a theoretical-error covariance built into the matter power spectrum, used in place of binary ell scale cuts. For a Euclid-like survey with ell_max = 5000, even multi-parameter baryon models can introduce significant bias. The theoretical error reduces the bias in Omega_m and S8 to acceptable levels with only a modest increase in variance, and it removes the need to choose an ell_max for each bin. Correction to the f-004 wording. Amon & Efstathiou (2206.11794) show that suppressing the non-linear power with A_mod~0.69 is sufficient to reconcile KiDS-1000 with Planck LCDM. It is one possible route, not the only one. On mitigation, Siegel et al. (2512.02954) find in their LSST-Y1 mock that an uninformed baryonification model removes the S8 bias but roughly doubles the S8 uncertainty (precision halved). A kSZ+eROSITA-calibrated prior recovers about half of that lost precision.
